title: Wisdom in a mystery; depths of God; taught by the Spirit words (1 Cor 2:6–15)
english: of this age, nor anything like the wisdom of the rulers of this age. At the same time he has made clear that the lessons circulating among others are not, in their origin, of humans but of invisible powers that are being abolished. And I would say that the poetic wisdom is of this age, and perhaps rhetoric too; and so is the wisdom that claims to speak about heaven and earth and the administration of the whole. So if we speak wisdom and say it among the perfect, we do not mean the wisdom of this age; for it is not through poems or through any such art. Origen: but we speak wisdom in a mystery—things unknown to the rulers of this age who work the wisdom of the wise of this world; and thus they did not know: they plotted against our Savior and Lord Jesus Christ and crucified him; for if they had known they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. Therefore wisdom must also be sought in the word—but after faith, after the way of life, according to what is written: “Desire wisdom; keep the commandments.”

On 1 Corinthians 2:9–11: “But as it is written, ‘What eye has not seen and ear has not heard and has not risen upon a human heart—what God prepared for those who love him.’ But to us God revealed them through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God. For who among humans knows the things of a human except the spirit of the human that is in him? So also no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God.” Origen: Scripture knows a difference between those who love God and those who fear God, and knows that those who love far surpass those who fear. Some things have been prepared also for those who fear; yet he prepared something greater for those who love than what was prepared for those who fear. For the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God. There is a Spirit that can search everything; the human soul cannot search everything, but a better Spirit had to come to be in us, so that when that Spirit is in us searching everything—even the depths of God—and is mingled with us, we may search together with it everything and the depths of God.

On 1 Corinthians 2:12–15: “Now we have not received the spirit of the world but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may know the things freely given us by God; which things we also speak not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual. But the soulish person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are folly to him, and he cannot know them because they are spiritually examined. The spiritual person examines all things, yet he himself is examined by no one.” Origen: let us understand the things freely given us by God; for if the Spirit from God that teaches us is not in us, we cannot say that we know the things freely given us by God—for no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God. “Which things we also speak,” he says, “not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit,” and what follows. All the wisdoms of this world are words taught by humans, which one learns in each of the rational arts; but they do not teach the things taught by the Spirit; and you would not say that the teacher, taught by the Spirit about what he says, taught them. For the Spirit present in the one who seeks and searches the truth shines in, and so always, by the renewal of the mind, he finds what he has not learned from humans. Therefore the Savior says, “Do not seek a teacher on the earth; for one is your Teacher, the Father in the heavens,” or “one is your Guide, the Christ.” A human sets down a few things—say Paul teaching Timothy—and Timothy, taking starting points, comes himself to the spring where Paul came and draws, and Timothy becomes equal to Paul.
